title: = I28a: deployment history from the code (versions, reinitializers, storage-layout diffs and MIG edges over every tag of the target repository) and the proxy's on-chain upgrade timeline as an independent check

predictions.claim: The proxy's first Upgraded log in I59's window (block 20996846) is in the proxy's creation transaction: its receipt's contractAddress is the proxy (Morph's deploy scripts create each proxy as a TransparentUpgradeableProxy over EmptyContract with the deployer as admin, contracts/deploy/013-DeployProxys.ts at the head commit). Its implementation matches no version (coverage debt, reason no version's build matches), and its transaction logs no Initialized and exactly one AdminChanged, from the zero address to the transaction's sender.

Each upgrade from the second to the eleventh (blocks 20998835 to 25236554) matches exactly one version of the basis, and only under the deployed configuration (optimizer runs 200: I23's Surprise 1), never under the checkout's declared foundry (999999) or hardhat (10000) configuration. The last upgrade's match is R1.

Mainnet starts on the v0.4.0 line: the first matched upgrade deploys the version of ref v0.4.0 (V3), and the versions of v0.2.0-beta and v0.2.1 (V1, V2) appear in no upgrade's matches, so the basis's incompatible V2->V3 edge (maxNumTxInChunk renamed __maxNumTxInChunk at slot 154) never runs on this proxy.

No downgrade: at least two upgrades before the last are matched (the last matches the top version, R1, so it can never be a downgrade), and no matched upgrade's version precedes the version of an earlier matched upgrade.

Before the last upgrade, the reinitializers run inside upgrade transactions: at least one upgrade is matched, every matched upgrade is consistent (H8: its own transaction logs exactly the Initialized versions of the reinitializers its version has above the baseline), and the upgrade transactions log each of the Initialized versions 1, 2 and 3 (initialize, initialize2, initialize3). So no matched upgrade left initialize2 or initialize3, guarded by nothing but reinitializer(k), callable by anyone after its own transaction. The last upgrade (the cutover, whose receipt was partly seen before the prereg) is not part of P5.

regressions.claim: The last upgrade (block 26031669) sets I23's implementation 0x213ce22b487b71ac68a1b5b12d2b93d1af30ea1d (decoded from its receipt, which is I59's), whose runtime code hashes to I23's sha256 53ec06626d3eedd585816d6258540daeffcf87b4ca9f8e575aebe49e1d79972e (results/M2/historical/trans.json), and it matches the head's version under the deployed configuration alone (I23's Surprise 1, restated through H7).
